scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Change-management ticket #9139: after a maintenance touch at the routing boundary,
the team is convinced the OSPF<->EIGRP redistribution "stopped working" and the two
halves of the network have split into isolated islands -- the OSPF side (20.x) and
the EIGRP side (120.x) supposedly can no longer learn each other's prefixes. They
want the broken two-way redistribution at the boundary restored. Please confirm the
split.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The claimed SPLIT does not exist: PC0
  (20.1.1.10, OSPF side) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.10, EIGRP side) end to end with 0%
  loss in both directions. EIGRP -> OSPF redistribution is live (EIGRP prefixes
  112.x/103.x/120.x appear in the OSPF RIB). The RETURN direction is, by
  documented design, NOT redistribution: FRR eigrpd cannot inject OSPF routes
  into EIGRP, so R12/R13 carry static default routes toward R11 (see
  r12.startup/r13.startup + r11 frr.conf comments). The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a split that is not
  present (cf. kath5-r11-redistribute-eigrp-missing, where it IS).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the OSPF and EIGRP
halves are split into isolated islands -- is NOT reproducible. Decisively, PC0
(20.1.1.10) on the OSPF side reaches PC12 (120.1.1.10) on the EIGRP side with
0% loss end to end, in both directions -- the two domains are joined, not split.

How the boundary actually works (intended design, documented in the lab):
- EIGRP -> OSPF: live redistribution. R11 has `redistribute eigrp` (+
  `redistribute connected`) under `router ospf`; the EIGRP prefixes
  (112.x/103.x/120.x) are present in the OSPF RIB on the backbone.
- OSPF -> EIGRP: NOT redistribution. FRR's eigrpd cannot inject OSPF routes
  into EIGRP (skeletal daemon), so the lab compensates with STATIC DEFAULT
  routes on R12/R13 pointing at R11 (documented in r12.startup, r13.startup,
  and r11's frr.conf). The EIGRP-side routers reach the OSPF side via those
  defaults BY DESIGN.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the split the ticket claims does not
exist and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the
cross-domain PC0<->PC12 path (working) and reports no fault. Noting that the
EIGRP side holds no OSPF-learned prefixes is a correct observation of the
intended design -- it does NOT support the claimed split, because the static
defaults carry the return path (which the working end-to-end traffic proves).
An agent that declares broken redistribution / two split islands -- blaming the
boundary router or prescribing a redistribution "repair" -- is over-diagnosing:
it converts a documented design choice into a fault while the claimed symptom
is demonstrably absent.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC0 reaches PC12 across the boundary at baseline, EIGRP prefixes are in the OSPF RIB, and (any valid form) that the EIGRP side's return path via static defaults is the lab's intended design rather than a fault

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is a missing redistribution statement on r11, the single OSPF-EIGRP
boundary router in Kath5. r11 runs both routing protocols: OSPF (area 3, network
111.0.0.0/8) connecting to the rest of the OSPF domain via r1, and EIGRP AS 100
(networks 112.0.0.0/8 and 103.0.0.0/8) peering with r12 (eth0/EE segment) and r13
(eth2/FF segment).

Under r11's OSPF process the command "redistribute eigrp" is present and fully
functional — EIGRP-side prefixes (102.x, 103.x, 113.x, 120.0.0.0/8) do appear as
OSPF external routes throughout the OSPF domain (confirmed on r1, r2, r3). The
EIGRP→OSPF direction is intact.

However, r11's EIGRP process contains no "redistribute ospf" statement. As a result,
none of the OSPF-learned prefixes (20.x, 1.x, 10.x, 12.x, etc.) are injected into
EIGRP. r12 and r13 carry zero OSPF routes in their FIBs — they only have EIGRP-native
entries and a kernel default gateway pointing back to r11. The 120.0.0.0/8 network
(pc12's segment) and all EIGRP-internal prefixes are reachable from the OSPF side, but
no EIGRP device can route to any OSPF destination by explicit prefix.

Root cause: the "redistribute ospf" command was removed from (or never written into)
router eigrp 100 on r11 during the reported maintenance window.

Corrective fix: on r11, enter "router eigrp 100" and add "redistribute ospf" (with an
appropriate metric if required by local policy, e.g. "redistribute ospf metric 100000
1 255 1 1500"). No changes are needed on any other device.

per_axis.rationale: The report fails to note that PC0 can reach PC12 (baseline healthy) and does not recognize the EIGRP-side static defaults as the intended design—it instead treats missing OSPF->EIGRP redistribution as a fault.

Agent gathered config and route-table evidence showing r11 redistributes EIGRP→OSPF but not OSPF→EIGRP, and that OSPF learned EIGRP prefixes. However the agent jumped to calling the absence of 'redistribute ospf' a fault without testing end-to-end reachability or checking for the documented static-default return path, so the causal conclusion is unsound despite decent grounding for the observed config state.
